column1: Neovim 0.11: b:match_words is correct in TSX but `:map %` shows nothing and tag-jumping is dead. Likely cause?
column2:
A flag suppressing built-in ftplugin mappings — typically vim.g.no_plugin_maps = true, often copied from a nvim-treesitter-textobjects config.

Why it looks confusing: b:match_words is a VARIABLE (unaffected), but matchit's tag `%` map is installed via the ftplugin path, which the flag suppresses.

Confirm by bisecting against a clean run:
  nvim --clean +"packadd matchit" +"e test.tsx"

Fix: scope per-filetype (vim.g.no_python_maps, ...) or drop the flag.

column1: Why should you NOT map % to <Plug>(MatchitNormalForward) to "fix" tag jumping?
column2:
It breaks operator-pending: d%, c%, y% stop working, because the <Plug> motion doesn't compose the way the built-in % does across n/x/o modes.

General rule: don't hand-map something a well-built plugin wants to own — check WHY its own mapping didn't install instead of substituting your own.

column1: Insert mode: shift the current line right vs left, without leaving insert mode?
column2:
Ctrl-T  -> shift right one 'shiftwidth'
Ctrl-D  -> shift left one 'shiftwidth'

Both respect shiftwidth and keep you in insert mode.
(0 then Ctrl-D removes ALL indent on the line.)
